competitors.name: mean_reversion
competitors.rules: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.

competitors.name: You
competitors.rules: Your real Robinhood account, rebased to the shared origin so it's comparable. Performance only — holdings and trades are deliberately not published.

competitors.name: congress_mirror
competitors.rules: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

regime.label: Policy and earnings event risk
regime.note: The Federal Reserve lists an October 27-28 FOMC meeting. Low confidence and 70% cash reflect policy risk, two near-term company events, rich screen leaders, and the analyst book's persistent negative all-time alpha.

analyst.thesis: Hold the October 14 target weights rather than churn after one mixed session. The latest settled session validated the cash buffer: the marked book fell 0.05% while SPY fell 1.08%, producing about 1.03 points of daily alpha, even though NEM fell 3.49%, because VRTX rose 2.74% and 70% remained in cash. The longer record is still poor: marked equity is $83.29, all-time alpha is about -20.3 points, and the prior 43-session annualized Sharpe was -3.54. The edge remains event-driven rather than trend-following. Newmont reports Q3 after the October 22 close, Vertex reports Q3 after the November 2 close, and FDA assigned November 30 as the povetacicept PDUFA target date. Robinhood data shows VRTX at 29.001949x trailing earnings and NEM at 14.087104x; the earnings calendar carries EPS estimates of $0.87 for VRTX and $1.93 for NEM. Keep VRTX at 16%, NEM at 14%, and 70% cash. This is the project's paper-portfolio bridge, not an official plugin investment recommendation.

evidence.point: The Federal Reserve lists a two-day FOMC meeting for October 27-28, 2026, with a press conference on October 28.
Vertex says FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date for povetacicept in IgAN; the supporting Phase 3 interim analysis showed a 49.8% UPCR reduction versus placebo with P<0.0001.
Vertex says it will report Q3 2026 results on November 2 after market close and host its call at 4:30 p.m. ET.
Newmont says it will release Q3 2026 results after market close on October 22 and hold its call at 5:30 p.m. EDT.
Robinhood's October 15 data shows VRTX at 29.001949x P/E, $130.8556 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income $1.0998 billion, and a $575.9630 mean analyst target.
Robinhood's October 15 data shows NEM at 14.087104x P/E, $118.5404 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $6.118 billion, Q2 net income $2.202 billion, and a $139.8879 mean analyst target.
At the October 14 settled close, VRTX was $498.50, NEM was $111.56, and SPY was $769.60; VRTX rose 2.74%, NEM fell 3.49%, and SPY fell 1.08% from October 13.

risks: VRTX faces a binary November 30 FDA decision; a delay, rejection, restrictive label, or adverse safety interpretation breaks the thesis.
NEM fell 3.49% in the latest session and remains below the paper entry; weak October 22 production or cost results can invalidate the valuation case.
The Robinhood analyst consensus is not an independent edge; both stocks can fall even if results meet consensus.
A 70% cash balance creates material opportunity cost if risk assets rally.
The persisted portfolio has about -20.3 points of all-time alpha and a -3.54 prior Sharpe; confidence stays low until realized results improve.

rationale.VRTX: [DATA] FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date for povetacicept, and Vertex confirmed Q3 results for November 2. The October 14 close was $498.50, up 2.74%; Robinhood reported P/E/PB of 29.001949/6.237380, Q2 revenue of $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income of $1.0998 billion, a $575.9630 mean analyst target, and a Q3 EPS estimate of $0.87. [ASSUMED] Approval can establish a nephrology franchise faster than the market credits, but the binary outcome and negative long-run portfolio alpha cap the anchor at 16%.
rationale.NEM: [DATA] Newmont confirmed Q3 results after the October 22 close; Robinhood's earnings calendar shows a $1.93 EPS estimate. The October 14 close was $111.56, down 3.49%; Robinhood reported P/E/PB of 14.087104/3.352210, Q2 revenue of $6.118 billion, Q2 net income of $2.202 billion, and a $139.8879 mean analyst target. [ASSUMED] Stable production and costs could beat the $1.93 consensus, but the price decline, below-entry position, and commodity risk cap the weight at 14%.

reflection.looking_back: The carried book ended October 13 at $83.33 with VRTX and NEM at 16% and 14% targets and 70% cash. Marked to October 14, the book slipped 0.05% while SPY fell 1.08%, producing about 1.03 points of daily alpha; VRTX rose 2.74% while NEM fell 3.49%.
worked: The 70% cash buffer and VRTX rebound limited the book's decline to 0.05% and beat SPY by about 1.03 points for the session.
Both positions retain company-confirmed, dated catalysts, so the theses remain falsifiable rather than momentum extrapolations.
missed: NEM fell 3.49% and remains below the paper entry, so the October 22 result now carries more downside risk.
One positive-alpha session does not repair about -20.3 points of all-time alpha or the prior -3.54 Sharpe.
reflection.adjustment: Hold VRTX at 16%, NEM at 14%, and cash at 70%; do not add a momentum-screen winner before the scheduled company events.

swarm.note: Live swarm — 109 fish, each a unique trader profile shown its own random ~20-name slice of the watchlist (with recent headlines), voted via OpenRouter. Independent-voter election; dissenters (ringed) chose CASH.

live.note: Real money — the Agentic cash account (••••), funded ~$100 on 2026-06-29, running the funded algorithms (100% momentum_breakout) via run-robin with a per-order confirm gate. Figures here are the real, unscaled account.

rules.momentum_breakout: Buy a 20-day-high breakout confirmed by above-average volume; exit when price closes below its 20-day SMA. Few big winners, many small losers.
rules.mean_reversion: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.
rules.blended_momo_rsi: Momentum breakout, but skip entries already overbought (RSI ≥ 70); exit on trend break or RSI > 75. Avoids chasing extended moves.
rules.deep_research_analyst: Holds the analyst's target weights; rebalanced each tick from a fresh research report (web + Robinhood data).
rules.llm_voters: Allocates across the swarm's top vote-getters (weight ∝ vote share, capped at 60%); rebalanced each tick.
rules.mirofish_real: Real-MiroFish: persona agents with memory interact over rounds, each ranking its best ideas; the panel's rank-weighted consensus (top 5 names, weight ∝ Borda points) rebalanced each tick.
rules.congress_mirror: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

sources.name: Standings, curves, decision trail (LIVE)

sources.name: Research analyst

sources.name: Swarm vote
sources.detail: Independent-voter election: 150 unique-profile cheap models (DeepSeek/Gemini/Llama/Haiku via OpenRouter) each read one shared briefing and return a single ballot; tallied in bot/swarm.py. No interaction between fish.

sources.name: Real-MiroFish swarm
sources.detail: Social-simulation swarm (bot/mirofish.py): persona agents with memory interact over multiple rounds — each re-ranks its best ideas seeing its own prior view and its neighbours' latest — so a consensus forms via peer influence (the opposite of the independent swarm). The panel's rank-weighted (Borda) consensus becomes a multi-name book (top 5 names, weight ∝ points). Tiered cost (cheap/default/qwen); seeded from the briefing + optional world-events news.

sources.name: Display scale
sources.detail: The real paper books are $100 each; every dollar and share figure on this site is shown ×100 (a $10,000 book) so holdings read in whole shares and dollars. Per-share prices and percentages are unscaled.

sources.name: Luck baseline
sources.detail: 200 seeded random 5-name equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolios from the same universe, same sessions — the shaded band on the chart is their 10th–90th percentile. A strategy that never leaves the band hasn't shown anything luck can't.

sources.name: Graduation bar
sources.detail: The standing rule before any strategy earns real money at scale: ≥60 forward sessions, ≥20 decisions, max drawdown better than −20%, and positive excess return vs S&P 500. Tracked live on this board.
